headline: The US defense research agency DARPA will give up to $300 million each to IBM, IonQ, Diraq and Atom Computing so their quantum computers can be tested by outside experts.
score_reason: Official government awards to major builders, but 'up to' amounts and no guarantee of success.
importance_line: Four of the leading quantum builders will have their machines checked by outsiders, which matters first to companies planning around quantum, then to the labs involved, though the awards guarantee no working machine.
summary: Network World reports that DARPA, the US defense research agency, is awarding up to $300 million each to IBM, IonQ, Diraq and Atom Computing to get their quantum hardware ready for independent testing, joining Microsoft and PsiQuantum in Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative. The program asks whether a vendor has a credible plan for a powerful enough quantum computer by 2033; analyst Bob Sutor, founder of Sutor Group Intelligence and Advisory, cautions that selection is no guarantee, and Google has chosen not to take part.
notes: Single outlet read in full; company executives quoted are interested parties.
